text:
maria: heads up — since last BMC firmware push (rollout window ~0200 UTC) we've seen a sharp uptick in GPU provisioning evictions in eu-west racks. heat sensors jumping ~6-8C and node fan RPMs stay pegged. provisioner backlog spiked and dedicated pools started falling back to hosted which is bleeding cost. :grimacing:
raj: can you paste the alert / sample node id?
maria: node id gk-eu-1143, alert: `oob:fan_rpm > 98% for 4m`, also saw `bmc_watchdog_reset_count` incrementing on the same nodes. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/d/infra/provisioning?view=evictions (shared) :eyes:
infra-bot: [ALERT] 1719420016 - gpu_eviction_rate increased by 4.2x in eu-west-1. Affected pools: dedicated-gpu-large (23 hosts), canary: dedicated-gpu-small (3 hosts).
jess: ugh. did we flip any thermal hysteresis or fan-control policy in this firmware? last patch notes said "improved therm margin handling" but no params listed.
daniel: Igrep'd the bmc syslog from gk-eu-1143 — attaching snippet:
```
Mar 26 02:07:11 bmc kernel: thermal_zone0: temp=82000 -> 88500
Mar 26 02:07:12 bmc ipmi: fan_control: set_mode automatic
Mar 26 02:07:16 bmc watchdog: reset_count=1
Mar 26 02:07:18 bmc sensor: sensor_reading: 92000
Mar 26 02:07:19 bmc ipmi: fan_pwm=100%
```
daniel: seems like sensors jump *then* fan pwm clamps to 100% and watchdog nudges. that matches the eviction timing.
anya: can we repro on canary? jess deployed the fw to canary last night right?
jess: yes, canary got the image. I can roll the canary back if we want to stop the footprint expanding.
raj: before rollback — can someone try toggling the fan-control profile to legacy on one of the canary nodes and see if temps stabilize? command via ipmitool:
```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H ${BMC_IP} -U admin -P *** raw 0x30 0x30 0x02 0xff  # set legacy fan mode
```
maria: started a manual change on gk-eu-1143 now. will report in 60s.
infra-bot: [ACTION] 1719420240 - live command executed by maria on gk-eu-1143
sre-oncall: FYI — if this keeps falling back to hosted we'll hit a $7k/day delta for eu-west traffic. ops budget is already flagged this month.
maria: after toggle — fans dropped to 65-70% and temps decayed ~4C in 45s. eviction didn't reoccur during the 10m window.
raj: that's telling. likely the new fw's thermal hysteresis thresholds are too tight or the fan PID is overly aggressive causing the BMC to hit watchdog on spike.
anya: can we capture full BMC nvram/var before rollback? need it for vendor ticket. also collect `ipmitool sdr list` and `ipmitool lan print` for the node.
jess: I'll freeze canary rollout and open a rollback ticket. also pinging firmware vendor (fwbridge) with logs. :phone:
daniel: assign runbook: 1) freeze canary 2) convert remaining canary hosts to legacy fan profile 3) collect BMC nvram + sdr + logs (script below) 4) vendor ticket with tags.
daniel: script (quick):
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
NODE=$1
ssh root@$NODE 'ipmitool sdr list > /tmp/sdr.txt; ipmitool lan print > /tmp/lan.txt; journalctl -u bmc -o short-precise > /tmp/bmc-journal.log; tar czf /tmp/bmc-dump-$NODE.tgz /tmp/sdr.txt /tmp/lan.txt /tmp/bmc-journal.log;'
scp root@$NODE:/tmp/bmc-dump-$NODE.tgz /tmp/
```
raj: I'll take 1-2 hosts for deeper triage and vendor repro. please add me to the vendor ticket.
sre-oncall: also add a quick mitigation in the provisioner — lower concurrency for eu-west dedicated pools by 30% for now to avoid mass-evictions while we triage. that should reduce rollback-to-hosted thrash and cost.
jess: done — paused rollout at 02:18 UTC and lowered concurrency for dedicated-gpu-large. ticket FW-4721 opened and vendor pinged.
maria: thanks. I'll collect the dumps and upload to the ticket. will follow up with RCA once vendor responds. :thumbsup:
